# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

<!-- cap-evolve:journal-append-below — add your Iteration entry under this line; do not edit anything above it -->

## Iteration cand_0001 — teach the agent to PERFORM the request (not write code text), inspect the whole sheet, and honor the output contract
- Changes I made (1 line per edit):
  - prompt.md "How to read the instruction" + worked example: macro/VBA/formula/SUMIFS words name the KIND of computation, never text to place in a cell → always perform the operation and write DATA VALUES. (cluster 1 — fixes 160-6, which wrote VBA source into A6:L11.)
  - prompt.md "What to write" + task_template step 1 INSPECT: answer_position is only WHERE to write; read the full sheet (max_row/col) and the area around the target; align to in-sheet labels. (cluster 2 — 53161 only read preview rows 0-9, missed the schedule table.)
  - prompt.md "Deletion/removal" + checklist: survivors compact UP to top of range, freed bottom cells blank. (cluster 3 — 160-6.)
  - prompt.md "Filling a computed grid": fill EVERY defined cell incl literal 0; undefined/trailing cells stay None, never "". (cluster 2 — 53161 filled 72/208 + padded "".)
  - prompt.md "Types" + checklist: preserve source type; whole numbers→int; keep date-like TEXT as text (no date coercion). (cluster 4 — 160-6 str-where-int/float.)
  - task_template: soft "verification code" round rewritten into an ordered INSPECT→PERFORM&WRITE→VERIFY procedure with a 4-item pre-finish checklist (structural, makes verify unavoidable).
- Expected effect + safety: 160-6 should now compact 3 survivor rows into r6-r8 with correct types instead of writing macro text (directly addresses its whole trace). 53161 gets its best shot (find schedule table, fill all 208 incl 0). Every edit is ADDITIVE / a contract clarification; 0 tasks currently pass among the controllable set, and the protected (infra-errored-but-known-passing) tasks 40467/47484/52216 are guarded by PRESERVE-type framing and DEFINED-grid scoping.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none exist (iteration 1/1 from seed; ./prior_iterations empty). Used verified cross-run gold-checked findings from auto-memory to source every rule.
- Refuted hypotheses NOT re-tried: "write an Excel FORMULA instead of a literal" — verified in a prior run to REGRESS 52216 & 53161 (all-or-nothing on recalc) and to defeat in-sandbox self-check (formula reads None). Kept the literal-values rule.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 53161's exact scheduling semantics (all-or-nothing per test case) — a mid-tier reader may still miss the computation even with full inspection; no wording guarantees it.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: if 160-6 accepts and 53161 still fails, 53161 likely needs a worked example of a schedule×category cross-tab computation, or is beyond the reader's tier — decide via its next trace, not more emphasis.
